pass_6016_correcting_a_hardcoded_value.consequence: the sequence is 3, 5, 7, not 1, 5, 7 -- and that changes everything
pass_6016_correcting_a_hardcoded_value.how_it_slipped: the same failure mode as the three prose-versus-output slips earlier this session -- a number written by hand next to a computation that would have produced it correctly

pass_6016_correcting_a_hardcoded_value.the_truth: in W(1,2) the symplectic form is nonzero on every pair of distinct nonzero vectors, so no two points are collinear and alpha = 3

pass_6017_the_law.note: at n=2 this coincides with the ovoid size q^2+1 = 5; above rank 2 there are no ovoids and yet the linear growth continues

pass_6018_the_proof.argument: a set of pairwise non-collinear points is a set of vectors u_1..u_k in F_2^(2n) with sp(u_i,u_j) = 1 for all i != j. Their Gram matrix under the symplectic form is J_k - I_k over F_2 -- zero diagonal, ones off-diagonal. That matrix has rank k over F_2 when k is even and k-1 when k is odd. The vectors span a subspace of F_2^(2n), so the Gram rank is at most 2n, giving k-1 <= 2n for odd k, hence k <= 2n+1
pass_6018_the_proof.attainment: the bound is attained at all four ranks tested, which the argument does not by itself give
pass_6018_the_proof.status: PROVED here, and by this session's repeatedly confirmed heuristic a four-line proof about a classical object means the result is classical. Recorded as proved-and-presumed-classical rather than as a discovery

pass_6019_what_it_does_to_the_thread.so_the_structure_question_sharpens: the rigid 1+3+3 stabiliser at W(3,3) and the apparently-full S_7 at W(5,2) are two points on a ladder whose SIZE is now completely known. What varies is not how big the optimum is but how much symmetry it carries
